contributions.text: I beg to move, That leave be given to bring in a Bill to require the use of closed-circuit television (CCTV) in nurseries; to make provision about the retention, storage, disclosure and review of such CCTV recordings; to make provision about minimum standards and auditing requirements for digital devices used to access CCTV recordings in such settings; and for connected purposes. This year, Vincent Chan was arrested and put in prison for 18 years for sexually abusing babies and young children while he was working in a nursery in my constituency. Police seized his devices and the devices of Bright Horizons nursery where he worked, and found tens of thousands of illicit, inappropriate sexual images. Some 1,500 of those images fell into category A, which is the most extreme sexual imagery. I have spent the last year working with affected parents whose children went to the nursery. They have said to me that sexual abuse is a parent’s worst nightmare in any situation, but it is a double blow when people have put their children in a safe haven and gone to work, thinking that they have created a home away from home where the children will be looked after, protected and nurtured and then r
contributions.name: Tulip Siddiq

contributions.text: I congratulate the hon. Member for Hampstead and Highgate (Tulip Siddiq) on bringing forward the ten-minute rule Bill and raising this very important subject. I am sure we are all four-square behind her and her constituents in relation to the suffering they have had to go through at the hands of a rogue in a rogue nursery. What I am going to say this afternoon is based on the fact that the world is full of people with good intentions, but the road to hell is paved with good intentions. The nursery system in this country is already a lot more expensive for parents than any other in the European Union. When it comes to the number of children or babies in individual nurseries, we have much higher supervision ratios, and I am concerned that in bringing forward this Bill, the hon. Lady is essentially bypassing the regulator we have put in place. Ofsted—the Office for Standards in Education, Children’s Services and Skills—is already obliged to look at the standards that apply in our nurseries. contributions.name: Sir Christopher Chope

contributions.text: Order. Please be seated. Let us be respectful. Every Member has the right to be heard. Sir Christopher, you are on the clock, and there are not many minutes left.
contributions.name: Chair

contributions.text: Thank you, Madam Deputy Speaker. I am tempted to take up the whole of the time just to satisfy the hon. Member for Sutton and Cheam (Luke Taylor) that I am in charge at the moment, but I am not going to do that. Instead, I will bring my remarks to a close by saying that we should have some proportionality. I fear that Members cannot say, without being interrupted, “Hang on a minute, why do we want to do more regulation and to impose more legislation when the regulators have failed?” We should be trying to ensure that the regulators are fit for purpose. When the hon. Member for Hampstead and Highgate brings forward her Bill—I will not press it to a Division, because I think it is the right of every Member to be able to bring forward a Bill, and I hope that it gets debated in due course—I will seek to make amendments to reflect my point of view. Question put (Standing Order No. 23) and agreed to. Ordered, That Tulip Siddiq, Dame Priti Patel, Nigel Huddleston, Sir Alec Shelbrooke, Bob Blackman, Munira Wilson, Mr Tom Morrison, Liz Saville Roberts, Olivia Bailey, Janet Daby and Matt Western present the Bill.
